propositions: Commit-history rewrite changes stored commit SHAs in compacted ledger entries, causing the verifier to misclassify authentic events as key-not-valid-at-era because it trusts non-null stored SHAs and does not resolve positions against the current history.

The verifier must treat a ledger commit_sha as a cache and prefer the commit resolved from the event position in the current history over the recorded SHA, retaining the recorded SHA only as a fail-closed fallback when position resolution fails.

A compacted ledger entry with a non-null pre-rewrite commit SHA must verify correctly against the commit resolved from its position after history rewrite, and live-event behavior, ledger schema, event bytes, and null-commit recovery must remain unchanged.

A real-Git history-rewrite regression must prove that after rewriting all reachable commits with identical trees, the verifier preserves the authentic event verdict and identical (event_uuid, verdict, grandfathered) multisets when commit SHAs are ignored.
